name: VAOPGCPREC 30-97, Aug 29, 1997, Entitlement to Special Monthly Compensation for Disarticulation of the Hips Following Preexisting Paraplegia
content:
Decision Assessment Document
VAOPGCPREC 30-97, Aug 29, 1997, Entitlement to Special Monthly Compensation for Disarticulation of the Hips Following Preexisting Paraplegia
Office of General Counsel Precedent Opinion


What the case is about

What level of special monthly compensation (SMC) should be awarded to a claimant with nonservice-connected paraplegia who is entitled to compensation under 38 U.S.C. § 1151 for disarticulation of the hips?

Impact on VBA

Regardless of preexisting paraplegia, SMC is payable at the rate prescribed in 38 U.S.C. § 1114(n) to a claimant who is entitled to compensation for bilateral disarticulation of the hips under 38 U.S.C. § 1151.

Summary on facts and findings

See OGC Precedent Opinion

summary: Regardless of preexisting paraplegia, SMC is payable at the rate prescribed in 38 U.S.C. § 1114(n) to a claimant who is entitled to compensation for bilateral disarticulation of the hips under 38 U.S.C. § 1151.
